repair.programName: Xcel Energy - Residential Energy Efficiency Rebate Programs

programGeography.notes: Treat DSIRE 1581 as Colorado-only. DSIRE search results identify this record as a Colorado Xcel residential efficiency rebate program, while separate DSIRE records exist for other Xcel geographies and should not be merged into this package. ([DSIRE][1]) ([DSIRE][2]) ([DSIRE][3])

overallDecision.decisionRationale: This can move from blanket suppression to production form-gated logic. Official Xcel sources confirm active Colorado heat-pump rebate pages, current heat-pump application deadlines, a digital rebate application path, and official regulatory heat-pump rate/timing changes. The exact 2025-2026 rebate table was located in an Xcel-branded current PDF hosted by a contractor rather than on an official Xcel static URL, so source confidence is medium rather than high; however, the current table is corroborated by official Xcel program pages and official Xcel regulatory filings for the core rates and two-year combo-bonus rule. The prior blanket $600 default must be removed and represented only as a separate conditional bonus. ([Xcel Energy][4]) ([Xcel Energy][5])

measureRepairs.measureName: Air sealing for Xcel electric-heat or natural-gas heating customer

formulaRepair.formulaText: 30% of eligible air-sealing project cost, capped at $400, for a Colorado residential customer who heats the home with electricity or natural gas provided by Xcel Energy and meets the 20% CFM50 reduction requirement.

requiredInputs.label: Xcel Energy Colorado residential electric or gas account
requiredInputs.whyNeeded: Confirms customer and service-territory eligibility.

requiredInputs.label: Home heating service provided by Xcel Energy
requiredInputs.whyNeeded: Separates the heating-customer formula from the cooling-only formula.

requiredInputs.label: Eligible air-sealing project cost
requiredInputs.whyNeeded: The rebate is a capped percentage of project cost.

requiredInputs.label: Modeled or verified CFM50 reduction percentage
requiredInputs.whyNeeded: The current table requires a 20% reduction in CFM50.

requiredInputs.label: Xcel participating contractor used
requiredInputs.whyNeeded: The Xcel summary indicates participating-contractor requirements for these measures.

calculationTraceTemplate: Verify Colorado Xcel residential account and heating-customer eligibility.
Verify air sealing meets the 20% CFM50 reduction requirement.
Calculate 30% of eligible cost.
Cap the result at $400.
Exclude from user-facing totals until cost and eligibility inputs are present.

measureRepairs.evidenceText: The current Xcel-branded 2025-2026 summary lists the air-sealing standard for heating customers as 20% CFM50 reduction and 30% of project cost capped at $400; Xcel's digital application requires invoices and equipment/specification documents.  ([Xcel Energy][6])
measureRepairs.reasoningNotes: The prior $200 heating-customer cap is superseded for current 2025-2026 logic by the current Xcel-branded summary. Because the full current table was not found on an official Xcel-hosted PDF URL, keep medium source confidence and show no amount until quote/invoice cost is known.
